definition: DMA (Direct Memory Access) is a term for the method by which an I/O device directly reads from or writes to system memory.

Capture information checked together with image pixels. The Request's metadata is provided as a ControlList, and the FrameMetadata of the FrameBuffer contains capture status, timestamps, number of bytes used, and so on. Whether the other fields of FrameMetadata are valid depends on the capture status.

FrameBuffer object representing the memory region where image data is stored. It provides the file descriptor, offset, and length of each memory plane, and per-frame metadata. The valid scope of the data and metadata varies depending on capture success, error, or cancellation.
This refers to the IPU3 color correction matrix algorithm.
Refers to the frame buffer object to which the texture is to be attached.
Refers to the green R shading coefficient in the lens shading correction table.
Refers to the green B shading coefficient in the lens shading correction table.
Uses the category and severity level specified by the caller.

This is an interface that connects the graphics API with the display, image, and buffer of the operating environment. This document covers the boundary where shared buffers are imported as graphics images.
A kernel subsystem that manages Linux graphics devices. DRM pixel formats identify the channel layout within a buffer.
A prefix used in identifiers of OpenGL-family graphics APIs. The GL formats in this document indicate the channel configuration of textures.

This is a synchronization signal that indicates when the buffer may be used. If a valid fence is attached to the request, the preparation stage waits for the signal. It is different from the request completion signal.

This is the request state that has not yet changed to completed or cancelled. It does not mean device processing has started, and if an earlier request is in this state, the return of later requests may also wait.
This is information that indicates the control items and ranges to be used with the camera. The control list of a request must reference that camera's information map.
This is the Stream connected to the current camera configuration. If a request buffer points to a stream from a different configuration, submission validation rejects it.

This is a separate module (.so) that contains the image quality algorithm. It reads the statistics sent by the ISP and calculates the ISP configuration values to use for the next frame. It is separated from the libcamera core so that manufacturers can provide it without publishing its source.

This is the processing unit that converts the raw (Bayer) data output by the sensor into an image usable for display. It performs black level correction, lens shading correction, white balance, demosaicing, and so on.
It is a libcamera component that replaces ISP processing with the CPU or GPU on devices without a hardware ISP. In the source code, it uses the names software_isp and softisp.
A collective term for automatic exposure (AE/AGC), automatic white balance (AWB), and automatic focus (AF). It is a representative algorithm that the IPA calculates.
An automatic exposure algorithm that sets exposure time and sensor gain to match scene brightness.
An algorithm that estimates the color temperature of the illumination and sets per-channel R, G, and B gains so that white appears white.
An algorithm that brings the image into focus by moving the lens position.

This processing corrects lens shading, the phenomenon where image edges are darker than the center or colors shift because of lens characteristics. It is applied by multiplying by a correction table that divides the screen into a grid.
This is the reference value the sensor outputs even when there is no light at all. This value is subtracted in the first stage of ISP processing.
This is a color filter array in which each sensor pixel records only one of R, G, or B. Raw data in this format must go through demosaicing before each pixel has RGB values.
This is the process of creating an RGB image from bayer raw data by interpolating each pixel's missing colors from neighboring pixels. It is also called demosaicing.
It is a small program that runs on a GPU. A software ISP can perform debayering and color correction with GPU shaders.
This is a YAML file containing the algorithm parameters for each sensor and platform (such as correction tables and color matrices). The IPA reads it when it starts.
This approach precomputes the results in a table and finds them directly from the input values. The LSC correction table corresponds to this case.
This is an unsigned fixed-point format. UQ<m, n> represents a value with m integer bits and n fractional bits.
This is how separate processes exchange messages. Because an unsigned IPA module runs in a separate process, libcamera calls it through IPC.

It is a proxy object that does not call the IPA module directly. It receives calls through the same interface and forwards them to an IPA thread or a separate process. It is automatically generated from mojom definitions at build time.
This is a file format that defines the functions and data types of the IPA interface. At build time, this definition is used to generate proxy code.

This is a libcamera component that finds the media devices of a specific hardware platform (such as IPU3 or RKISP1), creates cameras, queues requests to the devices, and returns completions. There is one for each platform.
This is a camera ISP included in some Intel laptop processors. libcamera has a Pipeline Handler and an IPA for this device.
It is a camera ISP included in Rockchip SoCs and NXP i.MX8MP, among others. libcamera has a Pipeline Handler and an IPA for this device.
This is the Arm Mali-C55 camera ISP. libcamera has a Pipeline Handler and an IPA for this device.
This processing straightens images distorted by the lens. The RKISP1 pipeline performs it by passing a vertex map (coordinate table) to the DW100 device.
A separate hardware device that corrects distortion by repositioning the image according to a coordinate table. It is found in NXP i.MX8MP and others.
This is the standard that USB webcams follow. libcamera handles this device using the uvcvideo Pipeline Handler.
An API the Linux kernel uses to handle cameras and video devices. libcamera controls sensor and ISP devices through this API.

It is a layer that lets the operating system handle hardware from different manufacturers through the same interface. The final target of application for this project is the in-house Android Camera HAL.

Standard error numbers that Linux functions use to report the cause of a failure. libcamera functions return this value as a negative number. For example, -ENODEV means no device, -EACCES means access denied, -EINVAL means invalid argument, -ENOMEM means out of memory, and -EXDEV means a resource belonging to a different object.
This is libcamera's debug check macro. In debug builds, if the condition is false, it logs a fatal message and stops execution.
This is the number of frames per second.
This is an environment that runs Linux on Windows. This site is produced from the results of building and extracting libcamera in WSL2.
This is the external documentation tool whose reading-screen layout and figure zoom and search rules this site referred to. It did not use the tool's runner; only its rules were applied.
When the buffer still has an unreleased fence, or when a buffer is already registered on the same stream, the -EEXIST error is returned.
This is the error code that indicates the IPC response-wait timer has expired. The timer setting value in this document is 2000ms.
This is the name of Intel's image processing unit family. Generation numbers are attached, as in IPU3 and IPU6.
This is a generation of the Intel Image Processing Unit (IPU). The official documentation lists it as a supported target of the simple pipeline, not as one with a dedicated handler.
It is a system-on-chip (SoC) from Rockchip. The official documentation lists it as a supported target of the rkisp1 pipeline handler.
This is the name for the most detailed diagnostic information among the log severity levels. Specifying `DEBUG` for the log level environment variable yields detailed logs.
When FrameBufferAllocator::allocate() is called again for a stream that already has allocated buffers, FrameBufferAllocator::allocate() returns -EBUSY.
RAW is a classification of pixel color encoding and is distinguished from StreamRole::Raw, a separate stream role for capturing raw sensor frames.
TID is the Linux thread ID returned by the gettid system call.
GNU is an operating system made of free software. Its name is a recursive acronym meaning GNU's Not Unix.
This is the GNU Compiler Collection, which includes front ends for C, C++, and others.
This is the GNU debugger that halts the program under the specified conditions and lets you inspect its execution state after it has stopped.

This is a 4:2:0 format that uses 8 bits per component. The first plane is luminance (Y), and the second plane contains interleaved chroma data in which Cb and Cr values are stored alternately, one each; the whole is placed in linearly contiguous memory.
This is a request proposing that the code changes be merged into the project.
The name of a Linux kernel driver that converts user-space memfd regions into dma-buf.

A virtual machine is a computer implemented in software by virtualizing the resources of a physical computer, and it runs its own operating system and applications. It is not limited to cloud servers and can also be created on a personal physical computer.
A Windows feature that lets you run a Linux environment on a Windows computer.
